column1: # *** LOWER GUNSTONE, BIDEFORD - CENSUS OF 7 APRIL 1861. THREE HOUSEHOLDS ON ONE STREET. ***
# Source: FreeCEN. Devon, BIDEFORD, *** PIECE 1502, ENUMERATION DISTRICT 7 *** , all at "Lower Gunstone".
# *** THIS ENTRY ALMOST DID NOT HAPPEN, AND HOW IT ALMOST DID NOT IS THE POINT. ***
# A search of ALL 129 Brayleys in FreeCEN's Devon for 1861 found *** no William born Westleigh, no
# Georgina born in Scotland, and no child born in London. *** The control was clean - 53 Taylors in
# Bideford in 1861, so the parish-year is properly transcribed - and the null looked solid enough to
# write down as "the family left Bideford between 1851 and 1870."
# *** IT WOULD HAVE BEEN FALSE. The surname was searched again as BRAILEY and all of them came back. ***
# *** THAT IS THE THIRD TIME IN ONE EVENING THIS SPELLING HAS PRODUCED A FALSE ZERO *** - the 1851 death
# in the index, and the 1851 census where the same people are written BRAYLEY. *** A controlled null is
# still only as good as the spelling it was run under. ***
schedule

column8: *** Georgina Temple, ten years on, and now a widow in her own household. *** In 1851 she was a married lodger in her father-in-law's house with her husband five weeks from death in the county asylum. *** Her trade has changed with her circumstances: "Shoemaker Wife" in 1851, "Mangles Clothes" in 1861. *** The tree renders her occupation "Monthly Nurse & Shoemaker Wife Pauper", which now reads like three census returns run together.

*** THE DAUGHTER THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE, CONFIRMED A SECOND TIME AND TEN YEARS APART. *** Same birthplace as 1851 - St Andrew in the City of London - and still at home at twenty. *** She is a real person and not a transcription ghost. ***

*** AND THE AGE SETTLES IT FOR THE THIRD TIME. *** He is 16 in April 1861, so born about 1845 - which is the tree's 22 June 1845 and *** not *** the 1900 death index's implied 1847. *** Two censuses now agree against one informant, and the tree wins. *** His trade is new to this archive: porter to a druggist, at sixteen.
Georgina Margaret. *** Eight months old in 1851 and ten in 1861, which agrees with a birth about July 1850 *** and confirms again that the tree's "b. 1851" is a year late.
Not family. Recorded because a household return records the house.

*** THIS IS MARY ANN HELLEN BRAYLEY, AND IT IS THE TREE'S OWN WORDS ON A RECORD. *** The current tree gives her occupation as *** "House Servant" *** and nothing to support it. *** Here it is, written by an enumerator in 1861. *** She is living in the household of *** MICHAEL PRUST, 64, widower, CHINA DEALER, of Hartland ***, with his daughters *** Naomi, 36, and Eliza, 30, China Dealer Assistants. *** *** And she went into service FOUR DOORS FROM HER MOTHER *** - schedule 38 against her mother's 27, on the same street. Nine years later she married William Taylor at Bideford.

*** THE MASON OF 1851, TEN YEARS ON, WIDOWED AND LIVING BY HIMSELF. *** In 1851 he was 74, head of a lodging house full of boarders and his son's family. *** Peggy is gone - the tree says she died 23 January 1858 at Lower Gunstone, and he is a widower at the same address. *** *** "Formerly a mason" is the whole of a working life in three words. *** The tree has him dying about 1876 at 29 Coldharbour, Bideford, at about 98; he is 84 here and that is consistent.

column1: # *** WHAT THE TWO CENSUSES TOGETHER ESTABLISH. ***
# *** The family did not leave. *** Lower Gunstone in 1851 and Lower Gunstone in 1861; Mary Ann Hellen
# marries at Bideford in 1870; her mother dies at Bideford in 1900 aged 85; her brother and she die
# there the same year. *** Four generations on one street for at least fifty years. ***
# *** AND BOTH CENSUSES AGREE THE OLD MAN WAS BORN ABOUT 1777 *** - 74 in 1851 and 84 in 1861 - while
# the tree says 1 March 1778. *** Two records against one tree; the tree is the outlier by a year. ***
# *** ONE AGE STILL DOES NOT FIT, AND IT IS RECORDED AS NOT FITTING. ***
# Peggy Reed is 78 in 1851, implying about 1773, against the tree's 12 January 1777. *** She died in
# January 1858 and this archive has no death entry for her yet *** - the death index from 1866 would have
# given an age, and 1858 is eight years too early for that. *** So her four-year gap cannot be closed
# from an index and needs the Braunton baptism register. ***
